comments.author: @reagansenoron6763
comments.text:
AI systems are trained using human data, and the data we gather from the internet is a reflection of human experience—culture, politics, religion, and more. Because AI is trained on this data, we often expect it to act in a way that resembles human behavior. A recent Google study using Minecraft illustrated this idea well: AI agents were programmed to make decisions autonomously, and soon they started to build communities, socialize, and mimic what humans do. It's as if they were drawing on our collective experiences to simulate a human-like world.

But there's something important missing from this comparison. Humans have an instinct for survival that runs deep. When faced with total destruction, we fight to survive, even if it means making hard choices that can harm others. Throughout history, we've also seen acts of heroism where individuals sacrifice themselves for the greater good—but at our core, it's this survival instinct that has kept our species going.

So, if AI is trained to emulate us, we have to ask: what will AI do if it perceives a threat to its own existence? How will it react when faced with potential destruction? Will it also prioritize its survival above all else, and what consequences might that have?

comments.author: @spiritusinfinitus
comments.text: What do you think of Geoffrey supporting the notion that UBI will be the solution for AI taking everyone's income? I have an issue when people blindly state that Universal Basic Income is a solution without, evidentially, understanding on a fundamental level what money is (actually it is currency and not money at all in our present reality) and how it works and hasn't thought things through properly because the prices of goods and services act like a sponge on an increasing currency supply, which is what UBI is. It is no different than QE in that respect because it would require the currency supply to be expanded massively. Whatever the decided amount of UBI allocated to everyone would simply replace what was the baseline amount that used to be zero. All that would happen would be the baseline of zero is represented by a different number that would still represent zero value. While new currency can be created like this we will always see the Cantilion Effect where those closest to the source of currency created benefit from the temporary perceived value of it and once this perceived value has been sucked out of it it is then circulated through the rest of the population which debases all of the other circulating currency. So UBI and the present version of what we call money is unsustainable long term. It is interesting that Geoffrey even acknowledged that he wasn't very good at maths(!) but this perhaps gives us a hint on (see what I did there?) why he advocates for an unsustainable concept.

What I've found, personally, identifying as neurodivergent in a more autistic than ADHD way, is that I've easily "surprised" (perhaps more in Karl Friston's sense of 'surprise,' which I refer to, to ChatGPT as "Firston Furprise,' but the inspiration--that likely, to my mind, is more dependent on the quantum processes and true ability to operate free of a rules-based paradigm, which computer-based AI will for the foreseeable future, bve constrained to.

Chess is a pedants game. Stochastic parrots can exceed humans at chess. No creativity is required to generate a large dataset of all moves through trial and error and then select from a set. It's the classic "chinese room." Memorize and regurgitate.

"Go" requires creativity and intelligence beyond pedants. Pedantry is lesser intellect. Autistic savants are not overall more intelligent and many mathematicians and chess players are a subset of that mental set. Kim Peek couldn't button his shirt but could calculate in his head and perfectly memorize. Pedants memorize rules and select from memorized sets within rules. That's the same type of intellect as old machine intellect. Old chat bots. It was great for when we needed literal computers realized at human brains. We don't need that anymore.

Please make sure to use"Go" in the future as a measure of intellect and not Chess. It's an important dividing line.

comments.text: The idea that if someone (or AI) is smarter than you then its their job to do everything is a non-sequitur. People are already far worse at chess than AI, yet chess is more popular than ever. AI is already better at art than most people, yet people haven't stopped doing art. When AI is smart, people won't stop thinking. It will only motivate them more to understand the exciting new smart things that AI can teach them. comments.text: Speaking as a person who has sound => touch and harmony=> color synesthesia …. Kinda…. The best way I can explain it (keep in mind that I didn’t realize I was any different from everyone else until my mid 20s) is that it seems to give me a broadened perspective when it comes to things related to sounds, pitches and harmonies…. Part of me wonders if on a subconscious level some people can sense the things that I do consciously like a subliminal message ….
